label: Attended NPL Executive Committee meeting
description: Hartree commented on Turing's ACE design efficiency compared to ENIAC.

sources.quote: The NPL Executive Committee would meet on March 19, 1946, and Turing was invited to present his report orally.

label: Published Nature article on ENIAC
description: Hartree reported on ENIAC to Nature.

sources.quote: Hartree had made almost the same point in his Nature article published on October 12, 1946 [11, p. 505].

label: Sent letter to The Times
description: Hartree criticized the term 'electronic brain' in a letter.

sources.quote: Hartree, who had recently moved from Manchester to Cambridge to take up his Plummer Chair of Mathematical Physics at the Cavendish Laboratory, sent a letter to The Times criticizing the newspaper's headline.

label: Delivered inaugural lecture at Cambridge
description: Hartree gave his inaugural lecture at the Cavendish Laboratory.

sources.quote: According to the Cambridge University Reporter, October 30, 1946, p. 231, the lecture was scheduled to place on November 13, 1946, at 4.45pm at the Cavendish Laboratory.

label: Moved to Cambridge
description: Hartree moved from Manchester to Cambridge to take up his Plummer Chair.

sources.quote: Hartree, who had recently moved from Manchester to Cambridge to take up his Plummer Chair of Mathematical Physics at the Cavendish Laboratory...

label: Published Calculating Machines book
description: Hartree published his inaugural lecture as a book.

sources.quote: [13] ——, Calculating Machines: Recent and Prospective Developments and their Impact on Mathematical Physics . Cambridge: University Press, 1947.

label: Published Calculating Instruments and Machines
description: Hartree published a book at the University of Illinois Press.

sources.quote: [15] ——, Calculating Instruments and Machines. Urbana: University of Illinois Press, 1949.

label: Delivered BBC lecture
description: Hartree gave a broadcast on automatic calculating machines.

sources.quote: At the climax of his BBC lecture on May 5, 1951 [19], Hartree admitted that digital computers could play games like chess...
